source.text: Ἀλλὰ ἐρεῖ τις· Πῶς ἐγείρονται οἱ νεκροί, ποίῳ δὲ σώματι ἔρχονται;

records.literal_gloss: But will say someone: How are raised the dead, with what kind and body do they come?

en.L: But someone will say, "How are the dead raised, and with what sort of body do they come?"
en.B: But someone will object, "How are dead people raised? And what sort of body will they have when they come back?"
en.R: But someone may ask, "How are dead people raised to life? What kind of body will they have?"

fr.L: Mais quelqu’un dira : « Comment les morts sont-ils ressuscités, et avec quel corps viennent-ils ? »
fr.B: Mais quelqu’un objectera : « Comment les morts sont-ils ressuscités ? Et quel corps auront-ils quand ils reviendront ? »
fr.R: Mais quelqu’un demandera peut-être : « Comment les morts peuvent-ils revenir à la vie ? Quel corps auront-ils ? »

es.L: Pero dirá alguno: «¿Cómo son resucitados los muertos, y con qué clase de cuerpo vienen?».
es.B: Pero alguien objetará: «¿Cómo resucitan los muertos? ¿Y qué clase de cuerpo tendrán cuando vuelvan?».
es.R: Pero alguien puede preguntar: «¿Cómo vuelven a la vida los muertos? ¿Qué clase de cuerpo tendrán?».

sw.L: Lakini mtu atasema, "Wafu hufufuliwaje? Na wanakuja na mwili wa aina gani?"
sw.B: Lakini mtu atapinga, "Wafu hufufuliwaje? Na watakuwa na mwili wa aina gani watakaporudi?"
sw.R: Lakini mtu anaweza kuuliza, "Wafu hufufuliwaje? Watakuwa na mwili wa aina gani?"

decisions.choice: someone will say: an imagined questioner whose objection Paul answers
decisions.reason: Paul uses a common way of arguing in his day: he puts a question in the mouth of an imagined opponent and then answers it (as in Romans 9:19). The question takes up the doubt of those in Corinth who said there is no resurrection of the dead (verse 12).

decisions.choice: two questions: how can the dead be raised at all, and what kind of body will they have
decisions.reason: The first question doubts that resurrection is possible; the second asks what body the dead could have once their bodies have decayed. Paul answers the second at length (verses 36-49), and in doing so answers the first. The present tenses ἐγείρονται ("are raised") and ἔρχονται ("do they come") speak of resurrection in general, not of something already happening.

decisions.choice: object (B); ask (R); will they have when they come back (B); will they have (R)
alternatives: with what body do they come
decisions.reason: The words introduce a question, so Balanced says "object" (m2) and Readable "ask". "Come" means to come back from death at the resurrection; Readable leaves it out because the question is plain without it.

decisions.choice: ressusciter, être ressuscité (L, B); revenir à la vie (R), through verses 35-58
decisions.reason: "Ressusciter" is the French word for the resurrection and takes the passive the Greek has ("les morts sont ressuscités", by God). Readable says "revenir à la vie", the plain words a young reader knows, as the English Readable says "raised to life".

source.text: ἄφρων, σὺ ὃ σπείρεις, οὐ ζῳοποιεῖται ἐὰν μὴ ἀποθάνῃ·

records.literal_gloss: Fool! you, what you sow not is made alive unless it dies;

en.L: Fool! What you yourself sow is not made alive unless it dies.
en.B: How foolish! A seed you sow does not come alive unless it dies.
en.R: How foolish you are! When you plant a seed, it does not come alive unless it first dies.

fr.L: Insensé ! Ce que tu sèmes, toi, n’est pas rendu vivant s’il ne meurt pas.
fr.B: Insensé que tu es ! La graine que tu sèmes ne prend vie que si elle meurt.
fr.R: Comme tu manques de bon sens ! Quand tu plantes une graine, elle ne peut pas prendre vie si elle ne meurt pas d’abord.

es.L: ¡Insensato! Lo que tú siembras no es vivificado si no muere.
es.B: ¡Qué insensatez! La semilla que siembras no cobra vida si no muere.
es.R: ¡Qué poco piensas! Cuando plantas una semilla, no cobra vida si antes no muere.

sw.L: Mjinga! Kile unachopanda wewe mwenyewe hakihuishwi kisipokufa.
sw.B: Ujinga ulioje! Mbegu unayoipanda haipati uhai isipokufa.
sw.R: Huo ni ujinga mtupu! Unapopanda mbegu, haiwezi kuota na kuishi isipokufa kwanza.

decisions.choice: fool: someone who is not thinking, who misses what is plain
decisions.reason: ἄφρων means without sense or understanding (Luke 12:20; 2 Corinthians 11:16-19). It is a sharp rebuke, of the kind used in the style of argument begun in verse 35, aimed at the imagined questioner, not at the Corinthians as a whole.

decisions.choice: you yourself: the questioner's own farming already answers the question
decisions.reason: The pronoun σὺ is not needed with the verb and so is emphatic: the one who asks how the dead can live sows seed and sees it every year.

decisions.choice: made alive: brought to new life, the verb Paul uses of the resurrection
decisions.reason: ζῳοποιεῖται is the verb of verse 22 ("in Christ all will be made alive") and verse 45 ("a life-giving spirit"). The seed is a picture of the body: life comes through death, as Jesus also said of a grain of wheat (John 12:24).

decisions.choice: Fool! (L); How foolish! (B); How foolish you are! (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep the rebuke but make it an exclamation, which sounds natural in English.

decisions.choice: A seed you sow (B); When you plant a seed, first (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the seed, which verse 37 makes explicit. Readable says "plant" for "sow" and adds "first" to show the order.

decisions.choice: Insensé ! (L); Insensé que tu es ! (B); Comme tu manques de bon sens ! (R)
decisions.reason: The word is a rebuke to someone who is not thinking (m1), not an insult about intelligence; "insensé" says exactly that. Readable puts it in everyday words. "Tu" because Paul answers one imagined questioner.

decisions.choice: insensato (L); qué insensatez (B); qué poco piensas (R)
decisions.reason: This is a different word from the foolishness of 1:18-25, where Spanish keeps "necio, necedad" and Readable "tonto, tontería"; here it means someone who is not thinking (m1), so Spanish says "insensato", keeping the two word families apart. The questioner is addressed as "tú", singular.

decisions.choice: Mjinga! (L); Ujinga ulioje! (B); Huo ni ujinga mtupu! (R)
decisions.reason: This is a different Greek word from the foolishness Paul sets against wisdom in chapters 1-3, which is "upumbavu" there, so here Swahili uses "mjinga, ujinga": someone who misses what is plain (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: hakihuishwi
decisions.reason: The verb "kuhuisha" (make alive) as in verse 22, since this is the word Paul uses of the resurrection (meaning decision); Balanced and Readable say the seed comes to life.

source.text: καὶ ὃ σπείρεις, οὐ τὸ σῶμα τὸ γενησόμενον σπείρεις ἀλλὰ γυμνὸν κόκκον εἰ τύχοι σίτου ἤ τινος τῶν λοιπῶν·

records.literal_gloss: And what you sow, not the body that will be you sow but a bare grain, if it may happen, of wheat or of some of the rest;

en.L: And what you sow, you do not sow the body that will be, but a bare grain, perhaps of wheat or of some of the rest.
en.B: When you sow, you are not sowing the body that will grow, but a bare seed, perhaps of wheat or of some other grain.
en.R: And what you plant is not the full-grown plant. It is only a bare seed, maybe wheat or some other kind of grain.

fr.L: Et ce que tu sèmes, ce n’est pas le corps qui sera que tu sèmes, mais un grain nu, peut-être de blé ou de quelque autre [plante].
fr.B: Quand tu sèmes, tu ne sèmes pas le corps qui va pousser, mais un simple grain, de blé peut-être, ou d’une autre céréale.
fr.R: Et ce que tu mets en terre, ce n’est pas la plante déjà grande. C’est seulement une graine toute nue, par exemple du blé ou une autre sorte de céréale.

es.L: Y lo que siembras, no siembras el cuerpo que ha de ser, sino un grano desnudo, quizá de trigo o de alguno de los otros;
es.B: Cuando siembras, no siembras el cuerpo que va a crecer, sino una simple semilla, quizá de trigo o de algún otro grano.
es.R: Y lo que plantas no es la planta ya crecida. Es solo una semilla, quizá de trigo o de otra clase de grano.

sw.L: Na kile unachopanda, hupandi mwili ule utakaokuwa, bali punje tupu, huenda ikawa ya ngano au ya [nafaka] nyingine.
sw.B: Unapopanda, hupandi mwili utakaoota, bali mbegu tupu, labda ya ngano au ya nafaka nyingine.
sw.R: Na unachopanda si mmea uliokwisha kukua. Ni mbegu tupu tu, labda ya ngano au ya aina nyingine ya nafaka.

decisions.choice: a bare grain: a seed without the stalk, leaves and ear it will have
alternatives: a seed with its husk removed
decisions.reason: γυμνὸν means naked or bare. The seed in the ground has none of the form of the plant that grows from it. The word prepares for the clothing language of verses 53-54, where the body "puts on" imperishability (compare 2 Corinthians 5:3).

decisions.choice: the body that will be: the plant that comes from the seed, the same life in a new form
alternatives: a different thing that replaces the seed
decisions.reason: Paul's picture holds two things together: what grows comes from what was sown, and yet it looks very different. So the resurrection body is joined to the present one, and yet is changed (verses 42-44).

decisions.choice: perhaps: for example
alternatives: "if it should happen" as a real condition
decisions.reason: εἰ τύχοι ("if it may happen") is a fixed phrase meaning "perhaps" or "for example", as in 14:10.

decisions.choice: the full-grown plant
decisions.reason: Readable says what "the body that will be" means in the picture of the seed (m2).

source.text: ὁ δὲ θεὸς δίδωσιν αὐτῷ σῶμα καθὼς ἠθέλησεν, καὶ ἑκάστῳ τῶν σπερμάτων ἴδιον σῶμα.

records.literal_gloss: The but God gives to it a body as he willed, and to each of the seeds its own body.

en.L: But God gives it a body as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} willed, and to each of the seeds its own body.
en.B: God gives it the body {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has chosen, and gives each kind of seed a body of its own.
en.R: Then God gives it the body {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has chosen for it. Each kind of seed gets its own kind of body.

fr.L: Mais Dieu lui donne un corps comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} l’a voulu, et à chacune des semences son propre corps.
fr.B: Dieu lui donne le corps qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a choisi, et donne à chaque sorte de semence un corps qui lui est propre.
fr.R: Ensuite, Dieu lui donne le corps qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a choisi pour elle. Chaque sorte de graine reçoit sa propre sorte de corps.

es.L: Pero Dios le da un cuerpo como {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} quiso, y a cada una de las semillas su propio cuerpo.
es.B: Dios le da el cuerpo que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} ha escogido, y a cada clase de semilla le da su propio cuerpo.
es.R: Luego Dios le da el cuerpo que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} ha escogido para ella. Cada clase de semilla recibe su propia clase de cuerpo.

sw.L: Lakini Mungu huipa mwili kama alivyotaka, na kila mbegu mwili wake wenyewe.
sw.B: Mungu huipa mwili aliouchagua, na huipa kila aina ya mbegu mwili wake.
sw.R: Kisha Mungu huipa mwili aliouchagua kwa ajili yake. Kila aina ya mbegu hupata aina yake ya mwili.

decisions.choice: God gives the body: the new form is God's gift, not something the seed makes for itself
alternatives: the seed grows into its body by nature alone
decisions.reason: The subject is God, set against "you" who sow (verses 36-37). The present δίδωσιν ("gives") speaks of God's work in every harvest. The same God gives the dead their new body.

decisions.choice: as he willed: by God's decision at creation, each kind with its own body
decisions.reason: The past tense ἠθέλησεν ("he willed") looks back to God's decision, most likely at creation, when plants were made to bear seed "each according to its kind" (Genesis 1:11-12). The list of creatures in verse 39 follows the same account.

decisions.choice: each kind of seed
decisions.reason: Paul means the different kinds of seed, each with its own plant; Balanced and Readable add "kind".

source.text: οὐ πᾶσα σὰρξ ἡ αὐτὴ σάρξ, ἀλλὰ ἄλλη μὲν ἀνθρώπων, ἄλλη δὲ σὰρξ κτηνῶν, ἄλλη δὲ σὰρξ πτηνῶν, ἄλλη δὲ ἰχθύων.

records.literal_gloss: Not all flesh [is] the same flesh, but one indeed of humans, another and flesh of beasts, another and flesh of birds, another and of fish.

en.L: Not all flesh [is] the same flesh, but one [is] of human beings, another flesh of beasts, another flesh of birds, another of fish.
en.B: Flesh is not all of one kind. Human flesh is one thing, the flesh of animals another, the flesh of birds another, and that of fish another.
en.R: Living things do not all have the same kind of flesh. People have one kind, animals have another, and birds and fish have others.

fr.L: Toute chair n’[est] pas la même chair ; mais autre [est celle] des êtres humains, autre la chair des bêtes, autre la chair des oiseaux, autre celle des poissons.
fr.B: Toutes les chairs ne sont pas de même nature : autre est la chair des êtres humains, autre celle des animaux, autre celle des oiseaux, autre celle des poissons.
fr.R: Les êtres vivants n’ont pas tous la même sorte de chair. Les humains en ont une, les animaux une autre, et les oiseaux et les poissons d’autres encore.

es.L: No toda carne [es] la misma carne, sino que una [es] la de los seres humanos, otra la carne de las bestias, otra la carne de las aves, otra la de los peces.
es.B: No toda carne es de una misma clase. Una es la carne de los seres humanos, otra la de los animales, otra la de las aves y otra la de los peces.
es.R: No todos los seres vivos tienen la misma clase de carne. Las personas tienen una clase, los animales otra, y las aves y los peces tienen otras.

sw.L: Si nyama yote [iliyo] nyama ile ile, bali [ipo] moja ya wanadamu, nyingine nyama ya wanyama, nyingine nyama ya ndege, nyingine ya samaki.
sw.B: Nyama si yote ya aina moja. Nyama ya wanadamu ni ya aina moja, nyama ya wanyama ni nyingine, ya ndege nyingine, na ya samaki nyingine.
sw.R: Viumbe hai havina aina moja ya nyama. Watu wana aina moja, wanyama wana nyingine, na ndege na samaki wana aina zao nyingine.

decisions.choice: flesh: the physical stuff of living bodies
decisions.reason: σὰρξ has many senses in Paul. Elsewhere in these letters it often means what is merely human (1:26; 3:3), but here it means the bodily flesh of people, animals, birds and fish. Paul's point is that God has made many different kinds of bodies.

decisions.choice: humans, beasts, birds, fish: the living creatures of the creation account
alternatives: a list with no particular source
decisions.reason: The four kinds recall the creatures of Genesis 1:20-26, named in the reverse order. κτηνῶν means animals, especially domestic animals and cattle.

decisions.choice: flesh
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for this word at Balanced and Readable is "by human standards", but that sense does not fit here (m1), so every level says "flesh".

decisions.choice: beasts (L); animals (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the older word; Balanced and Readable use the everyday one.

decisions.choice: la chair at every level; des êtres humains, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: As in English, the sense here is the physical stuff of bodies (m1), so the usual Readable paraphrase of this word does not apply. "Êtres humains" is set against animals, birds and fish and is already inclusive, so it needs no setting, as the English "human beings" has none.

decisions.choice: nyama
decisions.reason: Here the Greek word for flesh means the physical stuff of living bodies (meaning decision), which Swahili calls "nyama". "Mwili" is kept for the Greek word for body, which verses 35-44 set beside it.

source.text: καὶ σώματα ἐπουράνια, καὶ σώματα ἐπίγεια· ἀλλὰ ἑτέρα μὲν ἡ τῶν ἐπουρανίων δόξα, ἑτέρα δὲ ἡ τῶν ἐπιγείων.

records.literal_gloss: And bodies heavenly, and bodies earthly; but different indeed the of the heavenly glory, different and that of the earthly.

en.L: And [there are] heavenly bodies and earthly bodies; but the glory of the heavenly [is] one thing, and that of the earthly [is] another.
en.B: Some bodies belong to the heavens and some to the earth, and the glory of those in the heavens differs from the glory of those on earth.
en.R: There are bodies in the sky and bodies on the earth. The bodies in the sky have one kind of glory, and the bodies on the earth have another kind.

fr.L: Et [il y a] des corps célestes et des corps terrestres ; mais autre [est] la gloire des célestes, et autre celle des terrestres.
fr.B: Certains corps appartiennent au ciel, d’autres à la terre, et la gloire de ceux du ciel n’est pas celle de ceux de la terre.
fr.R: Il y a des corps dans le ciel et des corps sur la terre. Les corps du ciel ont une sorte de gloire, et les corps de la terre en ont une autre.

es.L: Y [hay] cuerpos celestiales y cuerpos terrenales; pero una [es] la gloria de los celestiales, y otra la de los terrenales.
es.B: Hay cuerpos que pertenecen al cielo y cuerpos que pertenecen a la tierra, y la gloria de los del cielo es distinta de la gloria de los de la tierra.
es.R: Hay cuerpos en el cielo y cuerpos en la tierra. Los cuerpos del cielo tienen una clase de gloria, y los de la tierra tienen otra.

sw.L: Na [kuna] miili ya mbinguni, na miili ya duniani; lakini utukufu wa [ile] ya mbinguni ni mmoja, na ule wa [ile] ya duniani ni mwingine.
sw.B: Kuna miili ya mbinguni na miili ya duniani, na utukufu wa ile ya mbinguni ni tofauti na utukufu wa ile ya duniani.
sw.R: Kuna miili angani na miili duniani. Miili ya angani ina aina moja ya utukufu, na miili ya duniani ina aina nyingine.

decisions.choice: heavenly bodies: the sun, moon and stars
alternatives: the bodies of the raised dead
decisions.reason: Verse 41 names the sun, moon and stars, so ἐπουράνια here means the bodies that are seen in the sky. Some have taken it as angels, but the next verse makes the meaning plain.

decisions.choice: glory: visible splendor, brightness and beauty
decisions.reason: δόξα can mean honor, but here it is the splendor that can be seen, the shining of the sun and the stars (verse 41). Paul uses the same word for the raised body in verse 43.

decisions.choice: belong to the heavens (B); in the sky (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the wording of heaven and earth; Readable says where the sun, moon and stars are seen.

decisions.choice: gloria
decisions.reason: "Gloria" is the key term for this word, and here it means visible splendor and brightness (m2); Spanish keeps "gloria" at every level through verses 40-43, as the English keeps "glory".

source.text: ἄλλη δόξα ἡλίου, καὶ ἄλλη δόξα σελήνης, καὶ ἄλλη δόξα ἀστέρων, ἀστὴρ γὰρ ἀστέρος διαφέρει ἐν δόξῃ.

records.literal_gloss: Another glory of sun, and another glory of moon, and another glory of stars, star for from star differs in glory.

en.L: One [is the] glory of [the] sun, and another [the] glory of [the] moon, and another [the] glory of [the] stars; for star differs from star in glory.
en.B: The sun has its own glory, the moon another, the stars another; and even among the stars, each has a glory that is different.
en.R: The sun shines with one kind of glory, the moon with another, and the stars with another. And each star shines with a glory different from the others.

fr.L: Autre [est] la gloire du soleil, et autre la gloire de la lune, et autre la gloire des étoiles ; car une étoile diffère d’une [autre] étoile en gloire.
fr.B: Le soleil a sa propre gloire, la lune une autre, les étoiles une autre encore ; et même entre les étoiles, chacune a une gloire différente.
fr.R: Le soleil brille d’une sorte de gloire, la lune d’une autre, et les étoiles d’une autre encore. Et chaque étoile brille d’une gloire différente de celle des autres.

es.L: Una [es la] gloria del sol, y otra [la] gloria de la luna, y otra [la] gloria de las estrellas; porque una estrella difiere de otra estrella en gloria.
es.B: El sol tiene su propia gloria, la luna otra, las estrellas otra; y aun entre las estrellas, cada una tiene una gloria distinta.
es.R: El sol brilla con una clase de gloria, la luna con otra y las estrellas con otra. Y cada estrella brilla con una gloria distinta de las demás.

sw.L: [Kuna] utukufu mmoja wa jua, na utukufu mwingine wa mwezi, na utukufu mwingine wa nyota; kwa maana nyota hutofautiana na nyota katika utukufu.
sw.B: Jua lina utukufu wake, mwezi una mwingine, na nyota zina mwingine; na hata kati ya nyota, kila moja ina utukufu tofauti.
sw.R: Jua hung'aa kwa aina moja ya utukufu, mwezi kwa aina nyingine, na nyota kwa aina nyingine. Na kila nyota hung'aa kwa utukufu tofauti na nyota nyingine.

decisions.choice: for star differs from star: even within one kind God has made variety
alternatives: a reason for the sentence before
decisions.reason: γὰρ ("for") adds a further example rather than a strict reason: not only do sun, moon and stars differ, but one star differs from another.

decisions.choice: the point is the variety of bodies God has made, preparing for the contrast in verses 42-44
alternatives: different levels of reward or glory for believers in heaven
decisions.reason: Paul is answering the question of verse 35, what kind of body the dead will have. The examples show that God can give a body of a quite different glory from the present one. The verse is not about ranks among the raised.

decisions.choice: shines with (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what the glory of the sun and stars is, their brightness (40 m2).

source.text: Οὕτως καὶ ἡ ἀνάστασις τῶν νεκρῶν.

records.literal_gloss: So also the resurrection of the dead.

en.L: So also [is] the resurrection of the dead.
en.B: It is the same with the resurrection of the dead.
en.R: This is how it will be when the dead are raised.

fr.L: Ainsi [en est-il] aussi de la résurrection des morts.
fr.B: Il en va de même pour la résurrection des morts.
fr.R: Ce sera comme cela quand les morts reviendront à la vie.

es.L: Así también [es] la resurrección de los muertos.
es.B: Lo mismo sucede con la resurrección de los muertos.
es.R: Así será cuando los muertos resuciten.

sw.L: Ndivyo ulivyo pia ufufuo wa wafu.
sw.B: Ndivyo ilivyo kwa ufufuo wa wafu.
sw.R: Ndivyo itakavyokuwa wafu watakapofufuliwa.

decisions.choice: so also: the seed and the different glories show what the resurrection is like
alternatives: only the last example, the stars
decisions.reason: Οὕτως ("so") draws the pictures of verses 36-41 together: as the plant differs from the seed and one body from another, the raised body differs from the body that died.

decisions.choice: resurrection: the dead raised to bodily life
decisions.reason: ἀνάστασις is the word of verses 12-13 and 21. It means rising up, and Paul speaks of it as something that happens to the body (verses 35, 44).

decisions.choice: when the dead are raised
decisions.reason: Readable turns the noun into a verb, which is easier to follow.

source.text: σπείρεται ἐν φθορᾷ, ἐγείρεται ἐν ἀφθαρσίᾳ·

records.literal_gloss: It is sown in decay, it is raised in imperishability;

en.L: It is sown in decay; it is raised in imperishability.
en.B: It is sown in decay; it is raised imperishable.
en.R: The body is put in the ground like a seed, and it decays. But it will be raised, and then it can never decay.

fr.L: Il est semé dans la corruption ; il est ressuscité dans l’incorruptibilité.
fr.B: Il est semé voué à la décomposition ; il est ressuscité impérissable.
fr.R: Le corps est mis en terre comme une graine, et il se décompose. Mais il reviendra à la vie, et alors il ne pourra plus jamais se décomposer.

es.L: Se siembra en corrupción; es resucitado en incorrupción.
es.B: Se siembra corruptible; resucita incorruptible.
es.R: El cuerpo se pone en la tierra como una semilla, y se descompone. Pero será resucitado, y entonces ya nunca podrá descomponerse.

sw.L: Hupandwa katika uharibifu; hufufuliwa katika kutoharibika.
sw.B: Hupandwa ukiwa unaharibika; hufufuliwa usioweza kuharibika.
sw.R: Mwili huwekwa ardhini kama mbegu, nao huoza. Lakini utafufuliwa, na hapo hautaweza kuoza kamwe.

decisions.choice: it is sown: the body is buried in death, like a seed put in the ground
alternatives: the body is "sown" at birth and through the whole of this life
decisions.reason: The subject is not named; it is the body (verses 35, 44). The picture of the seed that must die (verse 36) suggests that sowing means burial. Some take it to mean the whole present life, which is already marked by decay and weakness; verse 44, "it is sown a natural body", can be read either way.

decisions.choice: decay: being subject to decay and death; imperishability: being beyond decay
decisions.reason: φθορᾷ means decay or ruin, what happens to every living body. ἀφθαρσίᾳ is the opposite, what cannot decay (Romans 2:7; 2 Timothy 1:10). Paul is speaking of the body, not of sin.

decisions.choice: present tenses: what always happens, said of the resurrection as a sure thing
decisions.reason: Like the farmer's sowing (verses 36-37), the four pairs in verses 42-44 state what is true of every believer who dies and is raised.

decisions.choice: The body is put in the ground like a seed; it will be raised; it can never decay
alternatives: it is sown in decay, raised in imperishability
decisions.reason: Readable names the body, explains the picture of sowing (m1, which is uncertain) and uses verbs instead of the nouns. The future "will be" says what the present tense means here (m3).

decisions.choice: corruption, incorruptibilité, corruptible (L); décomposition, impérissable, périssable (B); se décomposer (R), through verse 54
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the traditional French words, which mean decay in this sense and let the Greek family be traced through verses 42-54. Today "corruption" most often means bribery, so Balanced says "décomposition" and "périssable / impérissable", and Readable uses the verb "se décomposer" (m2).

decisions.choice: corrupción, incorrupción (L); corruptible, incorruptible (B); se descompone, nunca podrá descomponerse (R) (verses 42-54)
decisions.reason: The words mean being subject to decay and death, and being beyond it (m2). Spanish "corrupción" and "incorrupción" name exactly this pair, and Literal and Balanced keep them through verse 54 ("lo corruptible", "incorrupción"); Readable says "descomponerse", as the English Readable says "decay".

decisions.choice: uharibifu, kutoharibika (L); unaharibika, usioweza kuharibika (B); kuoza (R)
decisions.reason: The pair "kuharibika / kutoharibika" (decay / be beyond decay) carries the Greek word family through verses 42, 50 and 52-54; Readable says "kuoza" (rot), the everyday word for what happens to a buried body.

source.text: σπείρεται ἐν ἀτιμίᾳ, ἐγείρεται ἐν δόξῃ· σπείρεται ἐν ἀσθενείᾳ, ἐγείρεται ἐν δυνάμει·

records.literal_gloss: It is sown in dishonor, it is raised in glory; it is sown in weakness, it is raised in power;

en.L: It is sown in dishonor; it is raised in glory. It is sown in weakness; it is raised in power.
en.B: In dishonor it is sown, in glory it is raised; in weakness it is sown, in power it is raised.
en.R: When it is buried, it has no honor, but it will be raised in glory. When it is buried, it is weak, but it will be raised with power.

fr.L: Il est semé dans le déshonneur, il est ressuscité dans la gloire ; il est semé dans la faiblesse, il est ressuscité dans la puissance.
fr.B: Dans le déshonneur il est semé, dans la gloire il est ressuscité ; dans la faiblesse il est semé, dans la puissance il est ressuscité.
fr.R: Quand il est enterré, il n’a plus aucun honneur, mais il reviendra à la vie dans la gloire. Quand il est enterré, il est faible, mais il reviendra à la vie plein de force.

es.L: Se siembra en deshonra; es resucitado en gloria. Se siembra en debilidad; es resucitado en poder.
es.B: En deshonra se siembra, en gloria resucita; en debilidad se siembra, en poder resucita.
es.R: Cuando se entierra, no tiene ninguna honra, pero será resucitado con gloria. Cuando se entierra, es débil, pero será resucitado con poder.

sw.L: Hupandwa katika aibu; hufufuliwa katika utukufu. Hupandwa katika udhaifu; hufufuliwa katika nguvu.
sw.B: Katika aibu hupandwa, katika utukufu hufufuliwa; katika udhaifu hupandwa, katika nguvu hufufuliwa.
sw.R: Unapozikwa, hauna heshima yoyote, lakini utafufuliwa katika utukufu. Unapozikwa, ni dhaifu, lakini utafufuliwa ukiwa na nguvu.

decisions.choice: dishonor: the shame and helplessness of death; glory: the splendor of the raised body
decisions.reason: ἀτιμίᾳ is lack of honor, the humiliation of a body that dies and is buried. δόξῃ is the glory of verses 40-41; Paul says the raised body will be like Christ's body of glory (Philippians 3:21).

decisions.choice: weakness: the frailty of the mortal body; power: the strength God gives in the resurrection
decisions.reason: ἀσθενείᾳ is the frailty of bodies that tire, fall ill and die. δυνάμει is the power of God that raised Christ (6:14; 2 Corinthians 13:4).

decisions.choice: When it is buried (R)
decisions.reason: Readable explains sowing as burial, following 42.s2 m1, which is uncertain.

decisions.choice: In dishonor it is sown, in glory it is raised (B)
alternatives: It is sown in dishonor; it is raised in glory
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the contrasting nouns first, where the stress falls when the verse is read aloud; the Greek sets them against each other at the end of each clause.

source.text: σπείρεται σῶμα ψυχικόν, ἐγείρεται σῶμα πνευματικόν.

records.literal_gloss: It is sown a body natural, it is raised a body spiritual.

en.L: It is sown a natural body; it is raised a spiritual body.
en.B: What is sown is a natural body; what is raised is a spiritual body.
en.R: The body that is buried has ordinary human life. The body that is raised will be given life by God's Spirit.

fr.L: Il est semé corps naturel, il est ressuscité corps spirituel.
fr.B: Ce qui est semé est un corps naturel ; ce qui est ressuscité est un corps spirituel.
fr.R: Le corps qui est enterré a une vie humaine ordinaire. Le corps qui reviendra à la vie recevra sa vie de l’Esprit de Dieu.

es.L: Se siembra un cuerpo natural; es resucitado un cuerpo espiritual.
es.B: Lo que se siembra es un cuerpo natural; lo que resucita es un cuerpo espiritual.
es.R: El cuerpo que se entierra tiene la vida humana de siempre. El cuerpo que resucita recibirá vida del Espíritu de Dios.

sw.L: Hupandwa mwili wa asili; hufufuliwa mwili wa kiroho.
sw.B: Kinachopandwa ni mwili wa asili; kinachofufuliwa ni mwili wa kiroho.
sw.R: Mwili unaozikwa una uhai wa kawaida wa kibinadamu. Mwili unaofufuliwa utapewa uhai na Roho wa Mungu.

decisions.choice: natural body: a body with ordinary human life, as people have it by nature
decisions.reason: ψυχικόν is the word of 2:14, built on ψυχὴν ("life, living being"), which verse 45 quotes from Genesis 2:7. It describes the body with the life Adam received at creation, the life every human being has. It is weak and mortal, but it is not evil.

decisions.choice: spiritual body: a body given life and ruled by the Spirit of God, not a body made of spirit
alternatives: a body made of a fine, heavenly substance
a body that is not physical
decisions.reason: Paul's adjectives of this kind say what something is marked by, not what it is made of: the "spiritual" person of 2:15 has God's Spirit, and the "spiritual" food and drink of 10:3-4 were real food and water given by God. The raised body is still a body; it is made alive by the Spirit, who already gives life to mortal bodies (Romans 8:11). Some read the word as describing a body made of spirit rather than flesh.

decisions.choice: natural body, spiritual body (L, B)
alternatives: a body with only natural life
decisions.reason: "Physical body" would suggest that the raised body is not physical, which m2 does not accept. In 2:14 Balanced says "a person who has only natural life"; here, set against "spiritual body" and taken up again in verse 46, "natural body" is clear.

decisions.choice: has ordinary human life; will be given life by God's Spirit
decisions.reason: Readable says what the two kinds of body are (m1, m2), as 2:14 does for the natural person.

decisions.choice: corps naturel, corps spirituel
decisions.reason: "Corps animal" and "corps psychique", the older French renderings, now suggest an animal body or a mental one. "Corps physique" would imply that the raised body is not physical, which m2 does not accept. "Naturel" says a body with ordinary human life (m1).

decisions.choice: cuerpo natural, cuerpo espiritual (L, B); la vida humana de siempre, vida del Espíritu de Dios (R) (verses 44-46)
decisions.reason: "Natural" is the word for this adjective in 2:14, and "espiritual" is a body given life by the Spirit, not one made of spirit (m2). "Cuerpo animal" would mislead, and "físico" would suggest the raised body is not a body; Readable explains both, as the English does.

decisions.choice: mwili wa asili, mwili wa kiroho (L, B); uhai wa kawaida, uhai kutoka kwa Roho (R)
decisions.reason: "Wa asili" (natural) as in 2:14, where the same Greek word is "mtu wa asili"; "wa kiroho" means given life by God's Spirit, not made of spirit (meaning decision), which Readable spells out as the English Readable does.

source.text: Εἰ ἔστιν σῶμα ψυχικόν, ἔστιν καὶ πνευματικόν.

records.literal_gloss: If there is a body natural, there is also spiritual.

en.L: If there is a natural body, there is also a spiritual [one].
en.B: If a natural body exists, a spiritual body exists too.
en.R: There is a body with ordinary human life, and so there is also a body given life by the Spirit.

fr.L: S’il y a un corps naturel, il y a aussi un [corps] spirituel.
fr.B: S’il existe un corps naturel, il existe aussi un corps spirituel.
fr.R: Il existe un corps qui a une vie humaine ordinaire. Il existe donc aussi un corps qui reçoit sa vie de l’Esprit.

es.L: Si hay cuerpo natural, hay también [uno] espiritual.
es.B: Si existe un cuerpo natural, también existe un cuerpo espiritual.
es.R: Hay un cuerpo con la vida humana de siempre, y por eso también hay un cuerpo que recibe vida del Espíritu.

sw.L: Ikiwa kuna mwili wa asili, kuna pia [mwili] wa kiroho.
sw.B: Ikiwa upo mwili wa asili, upo pia mwili wa kiroho.
sw.R: Kuna mwili wenye uhai wa kawaida wa kibinadamu, na hivyo kuna pia mwili uliopewa uhai na Roho.

decisions.choice: if: a real condition; since the one exists, so does the other
decisions.reason: Εἰ with the present states something both sides grant: there are natural bodies. Paul argues that there is also a spiritual body, and grounds it at once in Scripture (verse 45).

decisions.choice: and so (R)
decisions.reason: Readable states the condition as a fact, since it is one (m1).

source.text: οὕτως καὶ γέγραπται· Ἐγένετο ὁ πρῶτος ἄνθρωπος Ἀδὰμ εἰς ψυχὴν ζῶσαν· ὁ ἔσχατος Ἀδὰμ εἰς πνεῦμα ζῳοποιοῦν.

records.literal_gloss: So also it has been written: Became the first man Adam into a being living; the last Adam into a spirit life-giving.

en.L: So also it is written, "The first man Adam became a living being"; the last Adam [became] a life-giving spirit.
en.B: This is also what Scripture says: "Adam, the first man, became a living being." The last Adam became a spirit who gives life.
en.R: Scripture says, "Adam, the first man, became a living being." But Christ, the last Adam, became a spirit who gives life.

fr.L: Ainsi aussi il est écrit : « Le premier homme Adam est devenu un être vivant » ; le dernier Adam [est devenu] un esprit qui fait vivre.
fr.B: C’est aussi ce que dit l’Écriture : « Adam, le premier homme, est devenu un être vivant. » Le dernier Adam est devenu un esprit qui donne la vie.
fr.R: L’Écriture dit : « Adam, le premier homme, est devenu un être vivant. » Mais le Christ, le dernier Adam, est devenu un esprit qui donne la vie.

es.L: Así también está escrito: «El primer hombre, Adán, llegó a ser un ser viviente»; el último Adán, un espíritu que da vida.
es.B: Esto es también lo que dice la Escritura: «Adán, el primer hombre, llegó a ser un ser viviente». El último Adán llegó a ser un espíritu que da vida.
es.R: La Escritura dice: «Adán, el primer hombre, llegó a ser un ser viviente». Pero {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}, el último Adán, llegó a ser un espíritu que da vida.

sw.L: Vivyo hivyo pia imeandikwa, "Mtu wa kwanza Adamu akawa kiumbe hai"; Adamu wa mwisho [akawa] roho anayehuisha.
sw.B: Ndivyo Maandiko yanavyosema pia: "Adamu, mtu wa kwanza, akawa kiumbe hai." Adamu wa mwisho akawa roho anayetoa uzima.
sw.R: Maandiko yanasema, "Adamu, mtu wa kwanza, akawa kiumbe hai." Lakini Kristo, Adamu wa mwisho, akawa roho anayetoa uzima.

decisions.choice: Genesis 2:7, with "first" and "Adam" added
alternatives: the whole verse as a quotation
decisions.reason: Genesis 2:7 says that God breathed into the man the breath of life and the man became a living being. Paul adds πρῶτος ("first") and Ἀδὰμ ("Adam"). The second half of the verse, about the last Adam, is not in Genesis; it is Paul's own statement, set beside the quotation.

decisions.choice: a living being: a creature with natural life
alternatives: a soul as the inner part of a person
decisions.reason: ψυχὴν with "living" is a living creature. The word is the root of ψυχικόν ("natural") in verse 44: the natural body is the body Adam received at creation, before he sinned.

decisions.choice: the last Adam: Christ, the head of a new humanity
decisions.reason: As in verses 21-22 and Romans 5:14, Adam and Christ each stand at the head of a humanity. Christ is the "last" Adam because no other will follow. He became a life-giving spirit at his resurrection (Romans 1:4), when he began the life the raised will share.

decisions.choice: a life-giving spirit: the risen Christ, who gives the life of the Spirit
decisions.reason: πνεῦμα stands opposite ψυχὴν: Adam received life, Christ gives it. The risen Christ gives life by the Spirit (Romans 8:9-11; 2 Corinthians 3:17). Paul does not mean that Christ turned into the Holy Spirit, nor that he has no body; his point is the kind of life he has and gives. Some print "Spirit" with a capital, to show the link to the Holy Spirit.

decisions.choice: living being
decisions.reason: In English "soul" suggests the inner, non-bodily part of a person, which is not the sense (m2).

decisions.choice: spirit, lowercase
decisions.reason: The lowercase keeps the parallel with "living being" and avoids making Christ the same as the Holy Spirit (m4).

decisions.choice: But Christ, the last Adam (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names Christ (m3).

decisions.choice: Adam, the first man (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the name first, so that "the first man" reads as a description that prepares for "the last Adam".

decisions.choice: un être vivant; un esprit qui fait vivre (L), qui donne la vie (B, R), lowercase
decisions.reason: "Âme" would suggest the inner, non-bodily part of a person (m2). "Vivifiant" is the word-for-word form but is now rare; a relative clause says it plainly. Lowercase "esprit", as in English, so that Christ is not made the same as the Holy Spirit (m4). "Homme" here is Adam, a particular man, so it has no gender setting.

decisions.choice: está escrito (L); dice la Escritura (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the settled New Testament terms: "está escrito" at Literal, "la Escritura dice" at Balanced and Readable. "El primer hombre" names Adam, one particular man, so it takes no gender span.

decisions.choice: roho anayehuisha (L); roho anayetoa uzima (B, R)
decisions.reason: Lowercase "roho" as the English "spirit", but with personal agreement ("anaye-") because it names the risen Christ (meaning decision, footnoted). Literal keeps "kuhuisha" as in verse 22; Balanced and Readable use "uzima", the key term for life.

source.text: ἀλλ’ οὐ πρῶτον τὸ πνευματικὸν ἀλλὰ τὸ ψυχικόν, ἔπειτα τὸ πνευματικόν.

records.literal_gloss: But not first the spiritual but the natural, then the spiritual.

en.L: But the spiritual [is] not first, but the natural, then the spiritual.
en.B: The spiritual does not come first. The natural comes first, and the spiritual after it.
en.R: The body with ordinary human life comes first. The body given life by the Spirit comes later.

fr.L: Mais [ce n’est] pas le spirituel [qui vient] d’abord, mais le naturel, ensuite le spirituel.
fr.B: Ce n’est pas le spirituel qui vient en premier ; c’est le naturel, et le spirituel vient ensuite.
fr.R: Le corps qui a une vie humaine ordinaire vient en premier. Le corps qui reçoit sa vie de l’Esprit vient plus tard.

es.L: Pero no [es] primero lo espiritual, sino lo natural; después lo espiritual.
es.B: Lo espiritual no viene primero. Primero viene lo natural, y después lo espiritual.
es.R: Primero viene el cuerpo con la vida humana de siempre. El cuerpo que recibe vida del Espíritu viene después.

sw.L: Lakini si [mwili] wa kiroho ulio wa kwanza, bali ule wa asili, kisha ule wa kiroho.
sw.B: Mwili wa kiroho hautangulii. Mwili wa asili ndio wa kwanza, na ule wa kiroho unafuata baadaye.
sw.R: Mwili wenye uhai wa kawaida wa kibinadamu huja kwanza. Mwili uliopewa uhai na Roho huja baadaye.

decisions.choice: the spiritual, the natural: the two kinds of body of verse 44
alternatives: a general rule about spiritual things
decisions.reason: The neuter adjectives take up "natural body" and "spiritual body" from verse 44. Adam's body came first; the body like the risen Christ's comes after.

decisions.choice: the order is God's plan in history: first creation, then resurrection
alternatives: Paul is correcting a teaching that a heavenly, spiritual man came first
decisions.reason: Philo of Alexandria, a Jewish writer of Paul's time, read Genesis 1 and 2 as speaking of two men, a heavenly one made first and an earthly one made later. Paul may be answering such an idea, or he may simply be stating the order of God's work. Either way, the spiritual body belongs to the future, not to the present.

decisions.choice: The body with ordinary human life; the body given life by the Spirit (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names the two bodies, as in verse 44 (m1).

source.text: ὁ πρῶτος ἄνθρωπος ἐκ γῆς χοϊκός, ὁ δεύτερος ἄνθρωπος ἐξ οὐρανοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: The first man from earth, of dust; the second man from heaven.

en.L: The first man [was] from [the] earth, made of dust; the second man [is] from heaven.
en.B: The first man came from the earth and was made of dust; the second man comes from heaven.
en.R: The first man, Adam, was made from the dust of the ground. The second man, Christ, came from heaven.

fr.L: Le premier homme [était] de la terre, fait de poussière ; le second homme [est] du ciel.
fr.B: Le premier homme, tiré de la terre, était fait de poussière ; le second homme vient du ciel.
fr.R: Le premier homme, Adam, a été fait avec la poussière du sol. Le second homme, le Christ, est venu du ciel.

es.L: El primer hombre [es] de [la] tierra, terrenal; el segundo hombre, del cielo.
es.B: El primer hombre vino de la tierra y fue hecho de polvo; el segundo hombre viene del cielo.
es.R: El primer hombre, Adán, fue hecho del polvo de la tierra. El segundo hombre, {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}, vino del cielo.

sw.L: Mtu wa kwanza [alitoka] katika ardhi, wa mavumbi; mtu wa pili [anatoka] mbinguni.
sw.B: Mtu wa kwanza alitoka ardhini, akaumbwa kwa mavumbi; mtu wa pili anatoka mbinguni.
sw.R: Mtu wa kwanza, Adamu, aliumbwa kwa mavumbi ya ardhi. Mtu wa pili, Kristo, alikuja kutoka mbinguni.

decisions.choice: from the earth, made of dust: Adam formed from the ground
decisions.reason: Genesis 2:7 says God formed the man from the dust of the ground; Genesis 3:19 adds that to dust he will return. χοϊκός means "made of dust".

decisions.choice: from heaven: the risen Christ, whose origin and life are heavenly
alternatives: only Christ's coming into the world as a man
decisions.reason: In the setting of the resurrection body, "from heaven" most likely speaks of the risen Christ, who will come from heaven and change our bodies to be like his (Philippians 3:20-21; 1 Thessalonians 4:16). It may also include his coming as a man.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "the second man from heaven"
alternatives: "the second man is the Lord from heaven"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add the words "the Lord" after "second man", the reading of the King James Version. The shorter text is found in the earliest manuscripts; the addition looks like a copyist's explanation. Reviewers must check the apparatus.

decisions.choice: [was], [is] (L); came, comes (B); Adam, Christ (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek has no verb. Literal brackets the verbs and Balanced supplies them; Readable names the two men (m2 of verse 45).

decisions.choice: terrenal, del polvo (verses 47-49)
decisions.reason: The word means made of dust. Literal says "terrenal" here, after "de la tierra", and "el del polvo", "los del polvo" in verses 48-49, where the picture of dust is the point; Balanced and Readable say "hecho de polvo".

source.text: οἷος ὁ χοϊκός, τοιοῦτοι καὶ οἱ χοϊκοί, καὶ οἷος ὁ ἐπουράνιος, τοιοῦτοι καὶ οἱ ἐπουράνιοι·

records.literal_gloss: Such as the [one] of dust, such also the [ones] of dust, and such as the heavenly [one], such also the heavenly [ones];

en.L: As the [man] of dust [was], so also [are] those of dust; and as the heavenly [man is], so also [are] those [who are] heavenly.
en.B: Everyone made of dust is like the man made of dust, and everyone who belongs to heaven is like the man from heaven.
en.R: People made of dust are like Adam, the man made of dust. People who belong to heaven are like Christ, the man from heaven.

fr.L: Tel [était l’homme] de poussière, tels [sont] aussi ceux [qui sont] de poussière ; et tel [est l’homme] céleste, tels [sont] aussi ceux [qui sont] célestes.
fr.B: Tous ceux qui sont faits de poussière sont semblables à l’homme fait de poussière, et tous ceux qui appartiennent au ciel sont semblables à l’homme venu du ciel.
fr.R: Les gens faits de poussière sont comme Adam, l’homme fait de poussière. Ceux qui appartiennent au ciel sont comme le Christ, l’homme venu du ciel.

es.L: Como [es] el del polvo, así también [son] los del polvo; y como [es] el celestial, así también [son] los celestiales.
es.B: Todos los que son de polvo son como el hombre hecho de polvo, y todos los que pertenecen al cielo son como el hombre que viene del cielo.
es.R: Las personas hechas de polvo son como Adán, el hombre hecho de polvo. Las personas que pertenecen al cielo son como {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}, el hombre que vino del cielo.

sw.L: Kama alivyo yule wa mavumbi, ndivyo walivyo pia wale wa mavumbi; na kama alivyo yule wa mbinguni, ndivyo walivyo pia wale wa mbinguni.
sw.B: Wote walioumbwa kwa mavumbi ni kama yule mtu aliyeumbwa kwa mavumbi, na wote walio wa mbinguni ni kama yule mtu aliyetoka mbinguni.
sw.R: Watu walioumbwa kwa mavumbi ni kama Adamu, mtu aliyeumbwa kwa mavumbi. Watu walio wa mbinguni ni kama Kristo, mtu aliyetoka mbinguni.

decisions.choice: as ... so: those who belong to each man share his kind of being
decisions.reason: οἷος ... τοιοῦτοι ("of what sort ... of such sort") compares the two men with the people who belong to each. The verb is left out; verse 49 shows that the likeness to the heavenly man is fully received in the future.

decisions.choice: the heavenly ones: those who belong to Christ, the man from heaven
decisions.reason: ἐπουράνιοι is set against "those of dust", that is all human beings descended from Adam. The heavenly ones are believers, who belong to Christ now and will bear his likeness (verse 49; Philippians 3:20).

decisions.choice: the man (L, B); Adam, Christ (R)
alternatives: the one of dust, the heavenly one
decisions.reason: The adjectives refer to Adam and Christ (verse 47). Literal brackets "man"; Readable names them.

source.text: καὶ καθὼς ἐφορέσαμεν τὴν εἰκόνα τοῦ χοϊκοῦ, φορέσομεν καὶ τὴν εἰκόνα τοῦ ἐπουρανίου.

records.literal_gloss: And just as we wore the image of the [one] of dust, we will wear also the image of the heavenly [one].

en.L: And just as we have worn the image of the [man] of dust, we will also wear the image of the heavenly [man].
en.B: Just as we have worn the likeness of the man made of dust, so we will wear the likeness of the man from heaven.
en.R: We have had bodies like Adam, the man made of dust. In the same way, we will have bodies like Christ, the man from heaven.

fr.L: Et de même que nous avons porté l’image de [l’homme] de poussière, nous porterons aussi l’image de [l’homme] céleste.
fr.B: De même que nous avons porté l’image de l’homme fait de poussière, nous porterons aussi l’image de l’homme venu du ciel.
fr.R: Nous avons eu un corps comme celui d’Adam, l’homme fait de poussière. De la même manière, nous aurons un corps comme celui du Christ, l’homme venu du ciel.

es.L: Y así como hemos llevado la imagen del [hombre] del polvo, llevaremos también la imagen del celestial.
es.B: Así como hemos llevado la imagen del hombre hecho de polvo, llevaremos también la imagen del hombre que viene del cielo.
es.R: Hemos tenido cuerpos como el de Adán, el hombre hecho de polvo. De la misma manera, tendremos cuerpos como el {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}, el hombre que vino del cielo.

sw.L: Na kama vile tulivyovaa sura ya yule wa mavumbi, tutavaa pia sura ya yule wa mbinguni.
sw.B: Kama tulivyovaa sura ya mtu yule aliyeumbwa kwa mavumbi, ndivyo tutakavyovaa sura ya mtu yule aliyetoka mbinguni.
sw.R: Tumekuwa na miili kama ya Adamu, mtu aliyeumbwa kwa mavumbi. Vivyo hivyo, tutakuwa na miili kama ya Kristo, mtu aliyetoka mbinguni.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "we will wear", a statement about the future
alternatives: "let us wear", an appeal to live now as people of heaven
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads φορέσομεν, the future. A large number of manuscripts, including some of the oldest and most widely spread, read a form differing by one letter that means "let us wear". The two were pronounced alike in Paul's day, so copyists easily confused them. The future fits Paul's argument in verses 42-54, which describes what will happen rather than urging the Corinthians to act; the other reading has strong early support. Reviewers must check the apparatus.

decisions.choice: wear the image: share the likeness, as one wears clothing
alternatives: carry an image as a burden
decisions.reason: ἐφορέσαμεν means to wear, as of clothes worn regularly. The word anticipates "put on" in verses 53-54. εἰκόνα is the image or likeness: Adam's son was in his likeness (Genesis 5:3), and God means believers to be shaped into the image of his Son (Romans 8:29; 2 Corinthians 3:18).

decisions.choice: the image of the heavenly man: a body like the risen Christ's
decisions.reason: The setting is the resurrection body (verses 42-48), so the likeness meant here is bodily, as in Philippians 3:21.

decisions.choice: wear (all levels); likeness (B)
decisions.reason: "Wear" keeps the clothing picture of m2. Balanced says "likeness" because "wear the image" is not natural English.

decisions.choice: We have had bodies like Adam; we will have bodies like Christ (R)
alternatives: we have worn the image of the man of dust
decisions.reason: Readable says what the image is (m3) and names the two men.

decisions.choice: porter l’image (B)
decisions.reason: The English Balanced says "likeness" because "wear the image" is not natural English. "Porter l’image" is natural French, keeps the picture of clothing (m2) and the echo of man made "à l’image" of God, so Balanced keeps it.

decisions.choice: llevar la imagen
decisions.reason: The verb is used for wearing clothing, here sharing a likeness (m2). Spanish "llevar" is said of clothes and of a likeness alike, so Literal and Balanced keep "llevar la imagen".

decisions.choice: tulivyovaa ... tutavaa sura
decisions.reason: "Kuvaa" (wear, as clothing) keeps the Greek picture (meaning decision), which verses 53-54 take up again; "sura" is the likeness or image one bears.

source.text: Τοῦτο δέ φημι, ἀδελφοί, ὅτι σὰρξ καὶ αἷμα βασιλείαν θεοῦ κληρονομῆσαι οὐ δύναται, οὐδὲ ἡ φθορὰ τὴν ἀφθαρσίαν κληρονομεῖ.

records.literal_gloss: This now I say, brothers, that flesh and blood [the] kingdom of God to inherit not is able, nor the decay the imperishability inherits.

en.L: Now this I say, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, that flesh and blood cannot inherit [the] kingdom of God, nor does decay inherit imperishability.
en.B: What I mean, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, is this: flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God, and what decays cannot inherit what never decays.
en.R: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}, this is what I mean: our bodies of flesh and blood, as they are now, cannot receive God's kingdom. What decays cannot have a share in what lasts forever.

fr.L: Or je dis ceci, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} : la chair et le sang ne peuvent pas hériter du royaume de Dieu, et la corruption n’hérite pas non plus de l’incorruptibilité.
fr.B: Voici ce que je veux dire, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} : la chair et le sang ne peuvent pas hériter du royaume de Dieu, et ce qui se décompose ne peut pas hériter de ce qui ne se décompose jamais.
fr.R: {{gender:Frères et sœurs|Frères}}, voici ce que je veux dire : notre corps de chair et de sang, tel qu’il est maintenant, ne peut pas recevoir le royaume de Dieu. Ce qui se décompose ne peut pas avoir part à ce qui dure pour toujours.

es.L: Pero esto digo, hermanos: que la carne y la sangre no pueden heredar [el] reino de Dios, ni la corrupción hereda la incorrupción.
es.B: Lo que quiero decir, hermanos, es esto: la carne y la sangre no pueden heredar el reino de Dios, y lo corruptible no puede heredar lo incorruptible.
es.R: Hermanos, esto es lo que quiero decir: nuestros cuerpos de carne y sangre, tal como son ahora, no pueden recibir el reino de Dios. Lo que se descompone no puede tener parte en lo que dura para siempre.

sw.L: Basi nasema hivi, ndugu, kwamba mwili na damu haviwezi kuurithi ufalme wa Mungu, wala uharibifu haurithi kutoharibika.
sw.B: Ndugu, ninachomaanisha ni hiki: mwili na damu haviwezi kuurithi ufalme wa Mungu, wala kinachoharibika hakiwezi kurithi kisichoharibika.
sw.R: Ndugu, hivi ndivyo ninavyomaanisha: miili yetu ya nyama na damu, kama ilivyo sasa, haiwezi kuupokea ufalme wa Mungu. Kinachooza hakiwezi kushiriki katika kile kinachodumu milele.

decisions.choice: flesh and blood: human beings as they now are, mortal and weak
decisions.reason: "Flesh and blood" is a common expression for human beings in their weakness and mortality (Matthew 16:17; Galatians 1:16; Hebrews 2:14). Paul does not say that there will be no bodies in God's kingdom; he says that bodies as they now are, subject to decay, cannot enter it without being changed (verses 51-53).

decisions.choice: the second clause restates the first
alternatives: the second clause adds those who have died to the living
decisions.reason: "Decay" cannot inherit "imperishability": the same truth put in the words of verse 42. Both clauses lead to the need for the change of verse 51.

decisions.choice: inherit: receive as one's own share
decisions.reason: κληρονομῆσαι is the word of 6:9-10: God's kingdom is received as a gift, like an inheritance.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: The plural addresses the whole church, men and women.

decisions.choice: as they are now; receive; what lasts forever (R)
alternatives: flesh and blood cannot inherit; the perishable cannot inherit the imperishable
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that Paul means the present body (m1), says "receive" for "inherit" (m3), and turns "imperishability" into a plain phrase.

decisions.choice: {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}; capitalised at the start of a Readable sentence
decisions.reason: As in English, the whole church is addressed, women and men; "frères" stays available as the traditional form. Agreeing words follow the noun and need no span ("mes chers frères et sœurs").

decisions.choice: mwili na damu
decisions.reason: "Mwili na damu" is the Swahili way of naming human beings as they are now, mortal and weak (meaning decision), as in Hebrews 2:14; Readable speaks of "miili yetu ya nyama na damu" (our bodies of flesh and blood), as the English Readable.

source.text: ἰδοὺ μυστήριον ὑμῖν λέγω· πάντες οὐ κοιμηθησόμεθα πάντες δὲ ἀλλαγησόμεθα, ἐν ἀτόμῳ, ἐν ῥιπῇ ὀφθαλμοῦ, ἐν τῇ ἐσχάτῃ σάλπιγγι· σαλπίσει γάρ, καὶ οἱ νεκροὶ ἐγερθήσονται ἄφθαρτοι, καὶ ἡμεῖς ἀλλαγησόμεθα.

records.literal_gloss: Look, a mystery to you I tell: all not we will sleep, all but we will be changed, \v 52 in an instant, in a blink of an eye, at the last trumpet; it will sound for, and the dead will be raised imperishable, and we will be changed.

en.L: Look, I am telling you a mystery: not all of us will fall asleep, but all of us will be changed, \v 52 in an instant, in [the] blink of an eye, at the last trumpet; for it will sound, and the dead will be raised imperishable, and we will be changed.
en.B: Listen, I am telling you a mystery. Not all of us will die, but all of us will be changed, \v 52 in an instant, in the blink of an eye, when the last trumpet sounds. For the trumpet will sound, and the dead will be raised, never again to decay, and we who are alive will be changed.
en.R: Listen, I will tell you a mystery, something God has now made known. Not all of us will die, but God will change all of us. \v 52 It will happen in an instant, as fast as you can blink an eye, when the last trumpet sounds. Yes, the trumpet will sound, and the dead will be raised with bodies that can never decay. And those of us who are still alive will be changed.

fr.L: Voici, je vous dis un mystère : nous ne nous endormirons pas tous, mais tous nous serons changés, \v 52 en un instant, en un clin d’œil, à la dernière trompette ; car elle sonnera, et les morts seront ressuscités incorruptibles, et nous, nous serons changés.
fr.B: Écoutez, je vais vous dire un mystère. Nous ne mourrons pas tous, mais nous serons tous changés, \v 52 en un instant, en un clin d’œil, quand sonnera la dernière trompette. Car la trompette sonnera, et les morts seront ressuscités pour ne plus jamais se décomposer, et nous qui serons encore en vie, nous serons changés.
fr.R: Écoutez, je vais vous dire un mystère, un secret que Dieu fait maintenant connaître. Nous ne mourrons pas tous, mais Dieu nous changera tous. \v 52 Cela se passera en un instant, aussi vite qu’un clin d’œil, quand la dernière trompette sonnera. Oui, la trompette sonnera, et les morts reviendront à la vie avec un corps qui ne pourra jamais se décomposer. Et ceux d’entre nous qui seront encore vivants seront changés.

es.L: {{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}, {{plural_you:les|os}} digo un misterio: no todos dormiremos, pero todos seremos transformados, \v 52 en un instante, en un abrir y cerrar de ojos, en la última trompeta; porque sonará, y los muertos serán resucitados incorruptibles, y nosotros seremos transformados.
es.B: {{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}}, {{plural_you:les|os}} digo un misterio. No todos moriremos, pero todos seremos transformados, \v 52 en un instante, en un abrir y cerrar de ojos, cuando suene la última trompeta. Porque la trompeta sonará, y los muertos resucitarán para nunca más corromperse, y nosotros, los que estemos vivos, seremos transformados.
es.R: {{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}}, {{plural_you:les|os}} voy a contar un misterio, algo que Dios ahora ha dado a conocer. No todos moriremos, pero Dios nos transformará a todos. \v 52 Sucederá en un instante, en lo que dura un parpadeo, cuando suene la última trompeta. Sí, la trompeta sonará, y los muertos serán resucitados con cuerpos que nunca podrán descomponerse. Y los que todavía estemos vivos seremos transformados.

sw.L: Tazama, nawaambia siri: hatutalala sote, lakini sote tutabadilishwa, \v 52 katika kitambo kimoja, kufumba na kufumbua jicho, wakati wa tarumbeta ya mwisho; kwa maana [tarumbeta] italia, na wafu watafufuliwa wasioharibika, nasi tutabadilishwa.
sw.B: Sikilizeni, nawaambia siri. Hatutafariki sote, lakini sote tutabadilishwa, \v 52 papo hapo, kufumba na kufumbua, tarumbeta ya mwisho itakapolia. Kwa maana tarumbeta italia, na wafu watafufuliwa wasiharibike tena, nasi tulio hai tutabadilishwa.
sw.R: Sikilizeni, nitawaambia siri, jambo ambalo Mungu ametujulisha sasa. Hatutakufa sote, lakini Mungu atatubadilisha sote. \v 52 Itatokea ghafla, kufumba na kufumbua, tarumbeta ya mwisho itakapolia. Ndiyo, tarumbeta italia, na wafu watafufuliwa wakiwa na miili isiyoweza kuoza kamwe. Nasi tutakaokuwa bado hai tutabadilishwa.

decisions.choice: mystery: part of God's plan once hidden and now made known
decisions.reason: μυστήριον is God's purpose, hidden until he reveals it (2:7; Romans 11:25). The mystery here is what will happen to believers who are alive when Christ comes.

decisions.choice: fall asleep: die, said of believers
decisions.reason: κοιμηθησόμεθα is used of believers who have died (11:30; 15:6, 15:18, 15:20; 1 Thessalonians 4:13-15). It looks forward to waking at the resurrection.

decisions.choice: not all of us will die
alternatives: "all of us will not die", meaning none will die
decisions.reason: The negative stands next to πάντες ("all"), so it denies "all": some will die, but not everyone. All, living and dead, will be changed.

decisions.choice: in an instant, in the blink of an eye: the change will happen all at once
decisions.reason: ἀτόμῳ is what cannot be cut or divided, the smallest piece of time. ῥιπῇ is a quick movement, here of the eye: a blink or a glance.

decisions.choice: the last trumpet: the trumpet that announces God's final coming and the gathering of his people
alternatives: the last in a numbered series of trumpets
decisions.reason: In the Old Testament the trumpet announces the day of the Lord and the gathering of God's people (Isaiah 27:13; Joel 2:1; Zechariah 9:14). Jesus and Paul link it with the coming of the Son of Man and the raising of the dead (Matthew 24:31; 1 Thessalonians 4:16). "Last" means the one at the end.

decisions.choice: we: believers still alive at that moment, among whom Paul counts himself as one who may be
alternatives: Paul is certain he will be alive
decisions.reason: The "we" is set against "the dead", so it means those alive at Christ's coming, as in 1 Thessalonians 4:15-17. Paul speaks as one who may be among them; elsewhere he reckons with his own death (2 Corinthians 5:1-8; Philippians 1:20-23).

decisions.choice: will be changed: God will change them
decisions.reason: The passive ἀλλαγησόμεθα leaves God unnamed as the one who acts, as is common in Scripture; verse 57 names God as the giver of the victory.

decisions.choice: blink of an eye
decisions.reason: "Twinkling" is the traditional word, but in modern English it is used of stars. "Blink" is the movement Paul describes (m4).

decisions.choice: fall asleep (L); die (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the meaning of the idiom (m2), as at 11:30; Literal keeps the picture.

decisions.choice: something God has now made known (R); God will change (R); we who are alive (B); those of us who are still alive (R)
alternatives: a mystery; we will be changed
decisions.reason: Readable explains "mystery" (m1) and names God as the one who changes (m7). Balanced and Readable say who "we" are (m6).

decisions.choice: Look (L); Listen (B, R)
decisions.reason: ἰδοὺ calls for attention; "behold" is no longer used.

decisions.choice: imperishable (L); never again to decay (B); with bodies that can never decay (R)
decisions.reason: ἄφθαρτοι is the adjective of the noun in verse 42. Balanced and Readable say it with a verb, which reads more naturally after "raised".

decisions.choice: nous ne nous endormirons pas tous (L); nous ne mourrons pas tous (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Literal keeps the picture of falling asleep, which French also uses of death; Balanced and Readable give its meaning (m2). "S’endormir" rather than "dormir" because the verb says the moment of dying.

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}} (L); {{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word "look" is said to the whole church, so it is plural; Literal says "miren", as the settled terms do for speech, and Balanced and Readable "escuchen", as the English "Listen".

decisions.choice: dormiremos (L); moriremos (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 6: "dormir" for the idiom at Literal, "morir" at Balanced and Readable (m2).

decisions.choice: kufumba na kufumbua (jicho)
decisions.reason: "Kufumba na kufumbua" (shutting and opening the eye) is the Swahili idiom for something done in the blink of an eye, so it serves every level; Literal adds "jicho" (eye) as the Greek names it.

decisions.choice: hatutalala sote
decisions.reason: Swahili places "sote" after the negative verb to say "not all of us", which the Greek means (meaning decision); "sote hatutalala" would say "none of us will sleep".

source.text: δεῖ γὰρ τὸ φθαρτὸν τοῦτο ἐνδύσασθαι ἀφθαρσίαν καὶ τὸ θνητὸν τοῦτο ἐνδύσασθαι ἀθανασίαν.

records.literal_gloss: It is necessary for the perishable this to put on imperishability and the mortal this to put on immortality.

en.L: For it is necessary [that] this perishable [body] put on imperishability, and [that] this mortal [body] put on immortality.
en.B: This perishable body has to put on imperishability like a garment, and this mortal body has to put on immortality.
en.R: Our bodies that can decay must be clothed with a life that cannot decay. Our bodies that can die must be clothed with a life that never ends.

fr.L: Car il faut que ce [corps] corruptible revête l’incorruptibilité, et que ce [corps] mortel revête l’immortalité.
fr.B: Ce corps périssable doit être revêtu de ce qui ne périt pas, comme d’un vêtement, et ce corps mortel doit être revêtu de l’immortalité.
fr.R: Notre corps, qui peut se décomposer, doit être habillé d’une vie qui ne se décompose pas. Notre corps, qui peut mourir, doit être habillé d’une vie qui ne finit jamais.

es.L: Porque es necesario que esto corruptible se vista de incorrupción, y esto mortal se vista de inmortalidad.
es.B: Este cuerpo corruptible tiene que revestirse de incorrupción, como de un vestido, y este cuerpo mortal tiene que revestirse de inmortalidad.
es.R: Nuestros cuerpos, que pueden descomponerse, tienen que ser revestidos de una vida que no se descompone. Nuestros cuerpos, que pueden morir, tienen que ser revestidos de una vida que nunca termina.

sw.L: Kwa maana ni lazima [mwili] huu unaoharibika uvae kutoharibika, na [mwili] huu unaokufa uvae kutokufa.
sw.B: Mwili huu unaoharibika lazima uvae kutoharibika kama vazi, na mwili huu unaokufa lazima uvae kutokufa.
sw.R: Miili yetu inayoweza kuoza lazima ivikwe uzima usioweza kuoza. Miili yetu inayoweza kufa lazima ivikwe uzima usio na mwisho.

decisions.choice: it is necessary: it must happen in God's plan
decisions.reason: δεῖ speaks of what God has determined, as in verse 25 ("he must reign"). The change of verse 52 must happen because flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom (verse 50).

decisions.choice: put on: be clothed with, as with a garment
decisions.reason: ἐνδύσασθαι is the verb for putting on clothes. Paul pictures the body being clothed with imperishability, not thrown away. In 2 Corinthians 5:2-4 he uses the same picture of the new body put on over the old.

decisions.choice: this perishable, this mortal: this present body, the same body that is raised
decisions.reason: τοῦτο ("this") points to the present body, perhaps as if Paul pointed to himself. The body that is changed is the one that now lives and dies.

decisions.choice: mortal: able to die; immortality: being beyond death
decisions.reason: ἀθανασίαν means deathlessness. Only God has it by nature (1 Timothy 6:16); here he gives it to the bodies of his people.

decisions.choice: [body] (L); body, like a garment (B); our bodies, clothed with a life (R)
alternatives: this perishable must put on imperishability
decisions.reason: The Greek has neuter adjectives; the body is meant (m3). Balanced adds "like a garment" once, so that the picture of clothing is not missed (m2). Readable says what immortality is.

decisions.choice: esto corruptible, esto mortal, no brackets
decisions.reason: The Greek has neuter adjectives, "this perishable", "this mortal". Spanish can say the same with the neuter "esto", so Literal needs no supplied word where the English adds "[body]"; Balanced says "este cuerpo".

decisions.choice: kutokufa
decisions.reason: "Kutokufa" (immortality, being beyond death) is the word Swahili Romans 2:7 uses; it pairs with "kutoharibika" as the Greek pairs the two words.

source.text: ὅταν δὲ τὸ φθαρτὸν τοῦτο ἐνδύσηται ἀφθαρσίαν καὶ τὸ θνητὸν τοῦτο ἐνδύσηται ἀθανασίαν, τότε γενήσεται ὁ λόγος ὁ γεγραμμένος· Κατεπόθη ὁ θάνατος εἰς νῖκος.

records.literal_gloss: When but the perishable this puts on imperishability and the mortal this puts on immortality, then will come about the word that has been written: Was swallowed up the death into victory.

en.L: But when this perishable [body] puts on imperishability and this mortal [body] puts on immortality, then the word that is written will come about: "Death was swallowed up in victory."
en.B: When this perishable body has put on imperishability and this mortal body has put on immortality, then the words written in Scripture will come true: "Death has been swallowed up in victory."
en.R: When our bodies that decay are clothed with a life that cannot decay, and our bodies that die are clothed with a life that never ends, then what Scripture says will come true: "Victory has swallowed up death."

fr.L: Mais quand ce [corps] corruptible aura revêtu l’incorruptibilité et que ce [corps] mortel aura revêtu l’immortalité, alors s’accomplira la parole qui est écrite : « La mort a été engloutie dans la victoire. »
fr.B: Quand ce corps périssable aura été revêtu de ce qui ne périt pas, et ce corps mortel de l’immortalité, alors se réaliseront ces paroles de l’Écriture : « La mort a été engloutie dans la victoire. »
fr.R: Quand notre corps qui se décompose sera habillé d’une vie qui ne se décompose pas, et notre corps qui meurt d’une vie qui ne finit jamais, alors ce que dit l’Écriture se réalisera : « La victoire a englouti la mort. »

es.L: Y cuando esto corruptible se vista de incorrupción y esto mortal se vista de inmortalidad, entonces se cumplirá la palabra que está escrita: «La muerte fue devorada en victoria».
es.B: Cuando este cuerpo corruptible se haya revestido de incorrupción y este cuerpo mortal se haya revestido de inmortalidad, entonces se cumplirá lo que está escrito: «La muerte ha sido devorada por la victoria».
es.R: Cuando nuestros cuerpos que se descomponen sean revestidos de una vida que no se descompone, y nuestros cuerpos que mueren sean revestidos de una vida que nunca termina, entonces se cumplirá lo que dice la Escritura: «La victoria se ha tragado a la muerte».

sw.L: Lakini [mwili] huu unaoharibika utakapovaa kutoharibika, na [mwili] huu unaokufa utakapovaa kutokufa, ndipo litakapotimia neno lililoandikwa: "Kifo kimemezwa katika ushindi."
sw.B: Mwili huu unaoharibika utakapokuwa umevaa kutoharibika, na mwili huu unaokufa utakapokuwa umevaa kutokufa, ndipo maneno yaliyoandikwa katika Maandiko yatatimia: "Kifo kimemezwa katika ushindi."
sw.R: Miili yetu inayooza itakapovikwa uzima usioweza kuoza, na miili yetu inayokufa itakapovikwa uzima usio na mwisho, ndipo yale yanayosemwa na Maandiko yatatimia: "Ushindi umekimeza kifo."

decisions.choice: Isaiah 25:8, in a Greek form that differs from the Hebrew
alternatives: a saying with no Scripture behind it
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew of Isaiah 25:8 God is the subject: he will swallow up death forever, on the day he prepares a feast for all peoples. Paul's Greek is passive and says "into victory" where the Hebrew has "forever"; the Hebrew word for "forever" was also used for victory in later Hebrew and Aramaic. Paul's wording does not follow the Septuagint, which reads differently, but agrees with later Greek versions of Isaiah.

decisions.choice: was swallowed up: death completely done away with, by God
decisions.reason: The past tense Κατεπόθη describes the victory as finished. The passive leaves God unnamed, as the Hebrew names him. Death, which swallowed up the living, is itself swallowed up.

decisions.choice: then: the prophecy will be fully fulfilled at the resurrection
decisions.reason: τότε ("then") ties the fulfillment to the moment the dead are raised and the living changed. Death is not yet abolished (verse 26).

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: both clauses, perishable and mortal
alternatives: only the clause about the mortal
the two clauses in the other order
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts lack the first clause, about the perishable putting on imperishability, and a few put the clauses in the other order. Because the two clauses end alike, a copyist's eye could easily skip from one to the other. Reviewers must check the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Victory has swallowed up death (R)
alternatives: Death has been swallowed up in victory
decisions.reason: Readable makes the sentence active, which is easier to follow; it keeps the picture of swallowing.

decisions.choice: the words written in Scripture (B); what Scripture says (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the Scriptures, which the phrase "what is written" means.

decisions.choice: devorada (L, B); se ha tragado (R)
decisions.reason: The verb pictures death swallowed up and done away with (m2). "Devorar" keeps the picture in Literal and Balanced; Readable turns the sentence round, "la victoria se ha tragado a la muerte", as the English does.

source.text: ποῦ σου, θάνατε, τὸ νῖκος;

records.literal_gloss: Where of you, O death, the victory?

en.L: Where, O death, [is] your victory?
en.B: Death, where is your victory?
en.R: Death, where is your victory now?

fr.L: Où, ô mort, [est] ta victoire ?
fr.B: Mort, où est ta victoire ?
fr.R: Mort, où est-elle maintenant, ta victoire ?

es.L: ¿Dónde [está], oh muerte, tu victoria?
es.B: Muerte, ¿dónde está tu victoria?
es.R: Muerte, ¿dónde está ahora tu victoria?

sw.L: Uko wapi, ewe kifo, ushindi wako?
sw.B: Kifo, ushindi wako uko wapi?
sw.R: Kifo, ushindi wako uko wapi sasa?

decisions.choice: Hosea 13:14, adapted
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew of Hosea 13:14 the questions are "Where are your plagues, O death? Where is your destruction, O grave?" In Hosea they may call death's plagues down on Israel or mock death; the meaning there is debated. The Septuagint has "penalty" in the first question. Paul uses "victory", taking up the word of Isaiah 25:8 in verse 54, and makes these questions a taunt over defeated death.

decisions.choice: a taunt: death has no victory left
decisions.reason: The question needs no answer. Death is spoken to as an enemy (verse 26) that has lost.

decisions.choice: O death (L); Death (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the old form of address; Balanced and Readable simply name death. Readable adds "now" to show that the question mocks a defeated enemy (m2).

source.text: ποῦ σου, θάνατε, τὸ κέντρον;

records.literal_gloss: Where of you, O death, the sting?

en.L: Where, O death, [is] your sting?
en.B: Death, where is your sting?
en.R: Death, where is your sting now?

fr.L: Où, ô mort, [est] ton aiguillon ?
fr.B: Mort, où est ton aiguillon ?
fr.R: Mort, où est-il maintenant, ton dard ?

es.L: ¿Dónde [está], oh muerte, tu aguijón?
es.B: Muerte, ¿dónde está tu aguijón?
es.R: Muerte, ¿dónde está ahora tu aguijón?

sw.L: Uko wapi, ewe kifo, mwiba wako?
sw.B: Kifo, mwiba wako uko wapi?
sw.R: Kifo, mwiba wako uko wapi sasa?

decisions.choice: sting: the sting of a scorpion or insect, which wounds and kills
decisions.reason: κέντρον can be the sting of a scorpion (Revelation 9:10) or a farmer's goad (Acts 26:14). Here it is death's weapon, and verse 56 says what it is.

decisions.choice: death named again where Hosea has the grave
decisions.reason: The Hebrew of Hosea 13:14 speaks to "Sheol", the grave or the place of the dead, in the second question. Paul speaks to death both times.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "death" both times, victory first and sting second
alternatives: the two questions in the other order, with "grave" in place of "death" in the second
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts put the question about the sting first and speak to the grave (Hades) in the second, as the King James Version does. This brings the text closer to the Greek Old Testament. The earliest manuscripts support the SBLGNT. Reviewers must check the apparatus.

decisions.choice: O death (L); Death (B, R); now (R)
decisions.reason: As in the first question.

decisions.choice: aiguillon (L, B); dard (R); the same in verse 56
decisions.reason: "Aiguillon" is the French word for the sting of an insect or scorpion and the traditional one here; Readable says "dard", the everyday word for the part that stings (m1). "Piqûre" would name the wound rather than the weapon.

decisions.choice: aguijón
decisions.reason: The word is the sting of a scorpion or insect (m1); Spanish "aguijón" is that sting, and verse 56 keeps it.

decisions.choice: mwiba
decisions.reason: "Mwiba" is the sting of a scorpion or bee as well as a thorn, the thing that wounds and kills (meaning decision); "uchungu" (pain) would lose the picture, which verse 56 takes up.

source.text: τὸ δὲ κέντρον τοῦ θανάτου ἡ ἁμαρτία, ἡ δὲ δύναμις τῆς ἁμαρτίας ὁ νόμος·

records.literal_gloss: The and sting of the death [is] the sin, the and power of the sin [is] the law;

en.L: Now the sting of death [is] sin, and the power of sin [is] the law.
en.B: Death's sting is sin, and what gives sin its power is the law.
en.R: Death stings and kills people because of sin. And sin has power because of the law.

fr.L: Or l’aiguillon de la mort, [c’est] le péché, et la puissance du péché, [c’est] la Loi.
fr.B: L’aiguillon de la mort, c’est le péché, et ce qui donne au péché sa puissance, c’est la Loi.
fr.R: La mort pique et tue les gens à cause du péché. Et le péché a de la puissance à cause de la Loi.

es.L: Ahora bien, el aguijón de la muerte [es] el pecado, y el poder del pecado [es] la ley.
es.B: El aguijón de la muerte es el pecado, y lo que da poder al pecado es la ley.
es.R: La muerte pica y mata a la gente por causa del pecado. Y el pecado tiene poder por causa de la ley.

sw.L: Basi mwiba wa kifo [ni] dhambi, na nguvu ya dhambi [ni] sheria.
sw.B: Mwiba wa kifo ni dhambi, na kinachoipa dhambi nguvu yake ni sheria.
sw.R: Kifo huwachoma watu na kuwaua kwa sababu ya dhambi. Na dhambi ina nguvu kwa sababu ya sheria.

decisions.choice: sin is the sting by which death wounds and kills
decisions.reason: Death has its deadly power because of sin: sin came into the world through one man, and death through sin (Romans 5:12); the wages of sin is death (Romans 6:23).

decisions.choice: the law gives sin its power: it shows sin for what it is, stirs it up and condemns it
decisions.reason: Paul says briefly here what he explains in Romans 7:7-13: the law is holy (Romans 7:12), but sin uses the commandment to bring death, and the law counts sin against the sinner (Romans 5:13, 20). νόμος is the law given through Moses.

decisions.choice: what gives sin its power (B); sin has power because of the law (R)
alternatives: the power of sin is the law
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say how the law relates to sin; Readable also says what the sting does.

decisions.choice: la Loi, capitalised
decisions.reason: As the term sheet: the capital marks the Law of Moses, which is what gives sin its power here (m2), not law in general.

source.text: τῷ δὲ θεῷ χάρις τῷ διδόντι ἡμῖν τὸ νῖκος διὰ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: To the but God thanks, the [one] giving to us the victory through the Lord of us Jesus Christ.
